messages:
sam: Heads-up — I sketched a small API + console UX for a 'safety-first' rollout fallback order we discussed. Goal: during canaries/A-B we automatically prefer low-risk fallbacks first (regional failover -> capacity fallback -> model variant downgrade) unless customer opts into quality-first.

leah: short version: prefer failing over to same-variant in another region first, then reduce throughput (capacity), then swap to quantized/cheaper variant. agree? :thinking_face:

ana: annotate: customers with strict quality SLAs want model-variant fallback last. we should default to safety-first for PLG accounts. product needs an opt-in toggle.

mateo: small infra note — regional failover is cheaper for us if we already have warm pools. capacity fallback implies throttling/bursting semantics and interacts with quotas. we need a clear metric to trigger it (e.g., sustained 95th latency > X for Y sec).

sam: exactly. here's the draft rollout policy payload I put in the API proposal (console expresses same fields):

```json
{
  "policy_name": "safety_first_canary",
  "triggers": {
    "latency_p95_ms": 350,
    "duration_s": 30,
    "error_rate_pct": 2
  },
  "fallback_sequence": [
    {"type": "region_failover", "priority": 1},
    {"type": "capacity_throttle", "priority": 2, "params": {"max_qps": 0.7}},
    {"type": "model_variant_swap", "priority": 3, "params": {"variant": "quant-8bit"}}
  ],
  "quality_sensitivity": "safety_first", // other value: "quality_first"
  "telemetry_hooks": ["rollout.trigger", "fallback.executed", "fallback.recovered"]
}
```

leah: love the telemetry hooks. can we add a small event for each fallback attempt: fallback.attempt.{type} with outcome enum (ok/blocked/failed)? we need to show the console timeline.

sam: yep. will add. also thinking of adding a preflight check so model_variant_swap only happens if eval-run on a minibatch passes threshold. prevents silent quality regressions.

ana: question: should region_failover be multi-region or single standby region? customers in EU probably want EU-only failover for data residency. need a per-rollout constraint: allowed_regions list.

mateo: yep include allowed_regions in policy. infra will respect network/KMS constraints. also, capacity_throttle should optionally fall back to queued request behavior vs reject — include param: queue_window_s.

prod-bot: (deploy-check) rollout schema lint OK except missing fallback.attempt hook.

sam: updated draft: added fallback.attempt hook, allowed_regions, queue_window_s. Also added an explicit "abort_on_quality_degradation": true flag (overrides safety-first) so enterprise rollouts can stop at 1% quality regression.

leah: UX ask — console should show a compact 'rollout health' timeline: triggers -> attempted fallback steps with timestamps + diff of objective metrics (latency, error rate, eval-score). clickable to expand logs. :eyes:

mateo: ops note: when capacity_throttle is applied we must adjust billing/tokens metrics shown in console. otherwise customers see sudden cost-per-token jump because of queuing. add a billing_annotation field in telemetry.

ana: security/reg compliance: if model_variant_swap requires pulling a quantized model from public artifact repo, ensure attestation + allowed_artifact_sources check. add params.artifact_source_whitelist.

sam: good catch. I'll add that. final question for the group: fallback order — do we want region first always, or should we make fallback_order_pluggable and default to region-first but allow customers to reorder?

leah: make it pluggable. default to region-first for PLG. enterprise can reorder and set constraints.

mateo: +1. also suggest a dry-run mode where console simulates the fallback sequence without executing so SREs can verify.

sam: okay I'll update PR with pluggable order + dry-run + added telemetry events. expect a tiny prototype UI for console next week.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-2314 for infra changes (warm pool tagging + queue behavior).

leah: thanks. if nobody objects I'll merge the schema change tomorrow. please shout now if concerns. :thumbsup:

ana: no objections, just the artifact whitelist and eval preflight must be present before model swaps for enterprise.

sam: noted. merging tomorrow, will block model-variant swaps for enterprise until preflight is wired.

mateo: thanks all.
